The surge multiplier was 1.0x at quote time and 1.5x at the start of the trip (E-SRG-01); the quote of S$12.00 was binding at the multiplier in effect when it was given (Section 3.1) and the final fare is S$16.50. json.stance: The rider is owed the S$4.50 surge differential: the surge rose after the quote and nobody told the rider.
json.requested_outcome: refund of the S$4.50 surge differential
json.brief: The quote was S$12.00 at a 1.0x multiplier and the final fare was S$16.50 at 1.5x [E-PAY-01] [E-TRP-01]. The platform's own surge record shows the multiplier moved to 1.5x at 21:04:30, before the trip started at 21:05, and that the rider was not notified, with no method and no time recorded [E-SRG-01]. Section 3.2 requires an in-app notification before or at pickup. Section 3.3 gives a full refund of the surge differential, actual fare minus quote, when the rider was not notified, and Section 3.4 confirms the whole S$4.50 is surge: the surgeable subtotal is S$9.00 in both fares [E-PAY-01]. Precedent 7.2 refunded the whole differential on the same facts [Precedent 7.2].

arguments.point: The multiplier rose from 1.0x to 1.5x between the quote and the start of the trip, and the quote is binding at the multiplier in effect when it was given.
The surge record shows no notification to the rider, in the app or otherwise.
The whole S$4.50 is attributable to the multiplier, so Section 3.3 refunds it in full, as Precedent 7.2 did.

weaknesses.point: The rider only raised the fare at the end of the trip, after riding at the higher price.

json.stance: Surge pricing and the notification are the platform's, not the driver's; if a refund is due it must not be taken from the driver.
json.requested_outcome: no consequence for the driver; any refund paid by the platform
json.brief: The driver does not set the multiplier or send the surge notification; both sit in the platform's surge record [E-SRG-01]. Section 3.2 puts the notification duty on the platform ('the rider MUST be notified via an in-app notification'), so if the record shows none, the shortfall is the platform's. The driver accepts the figures: S$12.00 quote, S$16.50 final fare, a S$4.50 difference that is entirely the surge, with the booking fee exempt under Section 3.5 [E-PAY-01]. The chat shows the rider asked about the fare only after the ride [E-CHT-03]. The driver's request is that any refund of the differential be paid by the platform and not recovered from the driver.

arguments.point: The multiplier and the notification are platform functions recorded in the surge log; the driver took no action on either.
The rider first raised the fare after the trip ended, so the driver had no chance to explain it during the ride.

rebuttals.reply: Agreed on the figures; the change of multiplier is the platform's.
The record says not notified; the driver has no evidence to the contrary.
Accepted, provided the platform pays it.

concessions.point: The surge record shows the rider was not notified.
The full S$4.50 difference is the surge.
